name: Ukraine
note: Every fact is paraphrased from the quoted sentence of the linked source, and dated with that source's publication date. Run python scripts/verify_profiles.py to check each quote against its source.

facts.text: Civilian casualties remain at record levels: intensified Russian attacks in September continued a pattern of harm in 2026 far above previous years.
facts.quote: Civilian casualties in Ukraine remain at record levels, with intensified Russian attacks in September continuing a pattern of harm in 2026 far exceeding previous years, UN human rights monitors in Ukraine said on Friday.

facts.text: An estimated 10.8 million people across Ukraine need humanitarian assistance in 2026, including displaced and war-affected non-displaced people.
facts.quote: Overall, an estimated 10.8 million people across Ukraine will require humanitarian assistance this year, including internally displaced and war-affected non-displaced people.

facts.text: At least 328 civilians were killed and 2,105 injured in September 2026, 85% more than in September 2025.
facts.quote: At least 328 civilians were killed and 2,105 injured in September 2026, the highest for September since the start of the full-scale invasion, and 85 per cent higher than in September 2025 (249 killed; 1,068 injured).
facts.source: UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (OHCHR)

facts.text: From January to September 2026, 2,570 civilians were killed and 15,211 injured, 59% more than in the same period of 2025.
facts.quote: Civilian casualties from January to September 2026 (2,570 killed; 15,211 injured) were 59 per cent higher than in the same period in 2025 and more than twice as high as during same period in 2024.
facts.source: UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (OHCHR)

facts.text: In September 2026 civilians were killed and injured in 22 regions and Kyiv; the highest tolls were in Kyiv, Kherson, Sumy and Zaporizhzhia.
facts.quote: Civilians were killed and injured across 22 regions of Ukraine and the city of Kyiv. The highest numbers of killed and injured were documented in Kyiv (32 killed; 340 injured), where civilian casualties were recorded on 22 of 30 days, more frequently than in any previous month since the start of the full-scale invasion. Other cities heavily affected were Kherson (16 killed; 202 injured), Sumy (11 killed; 131 injured), and Zaporizhzhia (7 killed; 127 injured).
facts.source: UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (OHCHR)

facts.text: Of the 9.6 million people who have had to flee their homes, 3.7 million are displaced inside Ukraine.
facts.quote: Out of the 9.6 million people who have had to flee their homes, 3.7 million are internally displaced.

facts.text: About 1.45 million people who returned home now live in frontline districts.
facts.quote: Some 1.45 million returnees now live in frontline districts

facts.text: Strikes on 13 and 14 October 2026 hit Kyiv's three main power stations, temporarily leaving 600,000 people in the capital without electricity, according to Ukrainian authorities.
facts.quote: On 13 and 14 October, strikes hit multiple energy facilities, including Kyiv’s three main power stations, temporarily leaving 600,000 people in the capital without electricity, according to Ukrainian authorities.

facts.text: During the last cold season, only 32% of households in frontline districts could heat their homes adequately.
facts.quote: during the last cold season only 32 per cent of households could heat their homes adequately.

facts.text: In some regions up to 60% of people need health services and medicines, and as many as 90% urgently need financial aid.
facts.quote: In some regions, as many as 90% of people are in urgent need of financial aid, and up to 60% need health services and medicines.

facts.text: More than 4,200 educational institutions have been damaged since the war began, according to government estimates.
facts.quote: The Ukrainian Government estimates that between January and August of this year, hundreds more educational institutions were damaged, bringing the overall toll since the war began to over 4,200.

facts.text: Nearly 4.2 million children returned to school in September 2026.
facts.quote: This month, nearly 4.2 million children across Ukraine – and more than 366,000 teachers - returned to school.

facts.text: The UN and partners are appealing for US$2.3 billion in 2026 to help 4.1 million of the most vulnerable people.
facts.quote: The UN and partners appeal for US$2.3 billion in 2026 to assist 4.1 million of the most vulnerable people in Ukraine.
